items.text:
A small café with five employees uses custom-built software to manage its point of sale (POS) system. The system has the following functions:

  • Delete transactions.  

  • View daily sales data.

questions.title: The Interrelationships Between Hardware and Software (Q30, CSSA 2023)

items.text:
The Unicode Consortium was founded in 1991. Its method of representing characters in binary was extended to replace the existing ASCII code.

Explain why ASCII was no longer sufficient to serve this purpose and needed to be extended.

In your answer refer to the structure of ASCII and compare it with the structure of Unicode.

criteria.criterion: Explains the need for Unicode AND refers to the data structures of both ASCII and Unicode
Explains the need for Unicode OR describes the data structure of ASCII or Unicode

sampleAnswerContentItem.text:
ASCII was developed in the early days of computing as a standard way to represent American English. It only represented the letters of the alphabet and numbers as text. It also included various control codes for the hardware of the day. As such it only required 7 bits and represented 128 different characters.

With the global expansion of computing and communication, it became necessary to develop a worldwide system of coding which would have a single data item for every symbol used in the world. Unicode (utf8) uses 1 byte and incorporates the most used symbols. To preserve uniformity the first 128 characters of Unicode are identical to the ASCII set. Unicode also has larger datasets (2 byte, 3 byte etc.) and has plenty of room to include new symbols as they are created.

questions.title: Role of the Program Counter During Subroutine Execution (Question 33, ITE 2023)

items.text:
Consider the following algorithm.

1 BEGIN main

2 a = 1

3 b = 2

4 add(a,b,c)

5 print c

6 END main

7 BEGIN add(a,b,c)

8 c = a + b

9 END add

This algorithm is then coded in an appropriate language, compiled and run.
Describe how the program counter within the CPU is used throughout the execution of this program, with particular reference to the call to the subroutine and then returning to main.

criteria.criterion: Provides a comprehensive description of the use of the program counter in this program, showing an excellent understanding of the program counter and the stack
Provides a description of the use of the program counter in this program, with reference to the stack
Provides a response showing some understanding of the role of the program counter
Shows some understanding of the fetch execute cycle

sampleAnswerContentItem.text:
The program counter is a special register in the CPU which stores the memory address of the next instruction to be executed. When compiled, the high-level code above would be converted to a number of machine code instructions. A line such as c = a + b would actually be several lines of machine code.

When line 3 is being executed, the program counter would contain the address of the next instruction (line 4). Once the instruction in line 4 is fetched, the program counter is incremented to the next address in memory. However, line 4 requires the program to jump to the location in memory of the first machine code instruction in the subroutine add, this is accomplished by setting the program counter to this location. Note the current value in the program counter is first pushed onto the stack so that once execution of the subroutine add is finished, the value at the top of the stack is retrieved and placed back into the program counter. This means that the program can return to main at the correct position after executing the subroutine.

Note that memory locations associated with the parameters passed to the subroutine are also exchanged, however this is not directly related to the operation of the program counter.

Answers may include:

  • Cost effectiveness: Developers have traditionally had to purchase and provision their own infrastructure (such as servers) which can come at significant capital expense that may be beyond their financial capacity. With cloud computing, compute resources can be rented on-demand using a pay for what you use pricing model.
  • Agility: Sometimes developers may wish to experiment or try something, but do not want to invest in purchasing infrastructure such as servers for the purpose. With cloud, developers can spin-up compute resources in the cloud (usually very quickly) for the experiment and then shut it down and no longer be charged.
  • Capacity: Developers may be unsure how popular their application will become, or may be unsure about compute requirements if it's a new workload. This also has cost implications as developers no longer need to guess about capacity, and can instead match compute capacity to actual demand more closely.

questions.title: Understanding access modifiers and inheritance in object-oriented programming.(Q31BI-III, ITE 2024)*

items.text:
Consider the following pseudocode for the class BankAccount.

class BankAccount {
    private –
        balance: float
    public –
        createAccount(initialBalance):
            balance = initialBalance
        deposit(amount):
            balance = balance + amount
        withdraw(amount):
            IF amount > balance
                PRINT “Insufficient funds”
            ELSE
                balance = balance – amount
        getBalance():
            return balance
}
If the private and public modifiers were swapped, what effect would this have on the operation of the above BankAccount class? Use an example to support your response.

sampleAnswerContentItem.text:
If the private and public modifiers were swapped in the given BankAccount class, it would have a significant impact on its operation and violate the principles of encapsulation. In the original code, the `balance` attribute is declared as private, which means it can only be accessed and modified from within the BankAccount class itself. The public methods (for example, `createAccount`) provide a controlled interface to interact with the `balance` attribute, ensuring data integrity and enforcing any necessary validation or business rules.

If they were swapped, this kind of behaviour would be possible:

account = BankAccount() account.balance = 1000 # Direct assignment to public balance attribute

# Attempt to withdraw more than the balance

account.balance -= 2000 # No validation or business rules applied

# The balance is now -1000, which is an invalid state

# The private methods are not accessible from external code

account.withdraw(500) # This would raise an error

The SavingsAccount class should have an additional attribute interestRate and a method calculateInterest(interest) that calculates and adds the interest to the account balance based on the current balance and the given interest rate.

class SavingsAccount extends BankAccount:

            super(initialBalance)
            interestRate = rate
        calculateInterest():
            balance += balance * interestRate

items.text:
A BusinessAccount is a further type of BankAccount. It has all the features of a SavingsAccount with an additional overdraft feature. This means the account can be overdrawn by a pre-approved overDraw amount.

Write pseudocode for the BusinessAccount class.

criteria.criterion: Provides correct pseudocode to meet the requirements.

sampleAnswerContentItem.text:
class BusinessAccount extends SavingsAccount:
        private -
            overDraw: float
        public - 
            createAccount(initialBalance, rate, overdraftLimit):
                super(initialBalance, rate)
                overDraw = overdraftLimit
            withdraw(amount):
                IF amount <= (balance + overDraw)
                    balance -= amount
                ELSE
                    PRINT "Insufficient funds and overdraft limit exceeded"
            getOverdraftLimit():
                return overDraw
            setOverdraftLimit(newLimit):
                overDraw = newLimit
